Demi Moore's Sublime to Ridiculous Filmography: A Rollercoaster Ride Through Hollywood

From Striptease's 13% splat to The Substance's 90% fresh rating, Demi Moore's filmography is a rollercoaster of critical reception. Her latest, hailed as "career-best work," isn't just a comeback—it's a testament to her resilience in an industry quick to write off actresses of a certain age.

Originally published 17 September 2024 · RewindZone Archive

Actor & Director Profiles

Just when Hollywood thought it had Demi Moore figured out, she pulls the rug out from under us once again. Her latest film, The Substance, directed by Coralie Fargeat, has critics buzzing and audiences reeling.

...but this isn't just another notch on Moore's diverse filmography—it's a stark reminder of her enduring ability to surprise, shock, and captivate.

So, as we bask in the glow of Moore's latest success, let's take a journey through the highs, lows, and controversial moments that have defined her career. From the nostalgic charm of her Brat Pack days to the blockbuster success of the '90s, from critically panned choices to unexpected indie gems, Demi Moore's filmography is a masterclass in Hollywood survival.

Buckle up, cinephiles. This ride through Demi Moore's career is about to get bumpy, brilliant, and utterly unforgettable.

Reaching for the Stars: The Highs

Ghost (1990)

Advertisement
  • Box office: Over $500 million worldwide
  • Rotten Tomatoes: 75% critic score, 80% audience rating

Moore's breakout performance wasn't just a commercial success—it was a cultural phenomenon. Ghost proved that Moore could carry a film with both vulnerability and strength, cementing her status as a leading lady in Hollywood.

A Few Good Men (1992)

  • Rotten Tomatoes: 84% fresh rating

Holding her own against heavyweights like Tom Cruise and Jack Nicholson, Moore's turn as a naval lawyer proved she was more than just a romantic lead. Her performance contributed significantly to the film's critical acclaim.

The Hunchback of Notre Dame (1996)

  • Voice role as Esmeralda

Moore's voice work in this Disney classic revealed a softer side of her talent, surprising audiences and critics alike with her versatility.

Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery (1997)

  • Producer role

Stepping behind the camera, Moore demonstrated her savvy as a producer for this cult classic, showcasing her understanding of audience appeal beyond acting.

Margin Call (2011)

Advertisement
  • Rotten Tomatoes: 87% fresh rating

When many had written her off, Moore delivered a nuanced performance in this taut financial thriller, proving her ability to reinvent herself and remain relevant in a changing industry.

The Substance (2024)

  • Latest critical success

Stunning critics with her performance, Moore proved that even decades into her career, she still has the power to captivate audiences and deliver compelling performances.

Walking the Tightrope: The Controversial

G.I. Jane (1997)

  • Rotten Tomatoes: 53% critic score, 71% audience score

Moore's portrayal of the first woman to undergo Navy SEAL training was transformative. Despite mixed critical reception, many consider this a hidden gem in Moore's repertoire, showcasing her commitment to physically and mentally demanding roles.

Disclosure (1994)

  • Rotten Tomatoes: 59% critic score, 41% audience rating

This sexual harassment drama flipped gender roles, with Moore playing a predatory boss. The film sparked heated debates about workplace dynamics, proving Moore's willingness to tackle controversial subjects head-on.

When Stars Fall: The Lows

Striptease (1996)

  • Moore's record $12.5 million pay cheque
  • Rotten Tomatoes: 13% score

Meant to be her crowning achievement, Striptease instead became a cautionary tale. Despite the record-breaking pay cheque, the film's poor reception marked a low point in Moore's career.

The Scarlet Letter (1995)

  • Criticised for historical inaccuracies

This loose adaptation of Hawthorne's classic novel was criticised for its historical inaccuracies and Moore's anachronistic portrayal of Hester Prynne, highlighting the risks of reinterpreting beloved literature.

Wild Oats (2016) and Rough Night (2017)

  • Recent career missteps

These more recent misfires suggest that even decades into her career, Moore isn't immune to the occasional misstep. However, they also demonstrate her continued willingness to take risks and push boundaries.

Nostalgia's Warm Embrace: The Classics

St. Elmo's Fire (1985)

  • Rotten Tomatoes: 45% critic score, 63% audience rating

Despite lukewarm critical reception, this film's enduring audience appeal speaks to its status as a cult classic, marking Moore's entry into the iconic "Brat Pack" era of Hollywood.

About Last Night (1986)

  • Rotten Tomatoes: 65% fresh critic score, 60% audience score

Balancing critical approval with audience appreciation, this film cemented Moore's status as a rising star and showcased her ability to connect with viewers in relatable, contemporary roles.

The Final Cut

From the dizzying heights of Ghost to the controversial depths of Striptease, Demi Moore's filmography is a testament to her resilience, versatility, and unwavering commitment to her craft. While not every film was a critical darling, Moore's ability to reinvent herself and take on challenging roles has kept her relevant in an industry known for its fickleness.

As we look back on her career, it's clear that Demi Moore is more than just an actress; she's a Hollywood survivor. Her recent triumph in The Substance proves that even after all these years, she still has the power to surprise and delight audiences. In the end, it's not the individual scores that define Moore's career, but the bold, unapologetic way she's navigated the tumultuous waters of Hollywood.

Love her or hate her, one thing is certain: Demi Moore's cinematic journey has been anything but boring. And if The Substance is any indication, this rollercoaster ride is far from over. As Fred Topel of United Press International aptly puts it, "The Substance is provocative, but it only works because it is so entertaining." The same could be said for Moore's entire career—provocative, entertaining, and always, always worth watching.
